# Adopt v1.3.0

This release introduces the Precise visual defaults, a Reference workbench, optional accent palettes, and flat icon artwork. Existing semantic role names, exports, supported runtimes, and default theme colors remain intact. Read the [release process](../releases.md) before updating consumers to a new tag.

## Visual defaults

| Token | v1.2.0 | v1.3.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control / button radius | 8 / 9px | 4 / 4px |
| Card / dialog radius | 12 / 16px | 8 / 12px |
| Display | 40/44, weight 700 | 36/40, weight 500 |
| Body | 16/24 | 15/23 |
| Control / panel motion | 160 / 240ms | 140 / 200ms |

The charcoal/sage/mint default theme maps and base brand colors are unchanged. Rebuild generated or vendored adapters from the selected release; inspect real text wrapping, control spacing, responsive layouts, and reduced motion after adopting the new dimensions.

## Optional accent palettes

Sage retains the original sage/mint default. Ember, Slate, Royal, Amber, and Monochrome only override accent, link, focus, selection, and informational roles. Surface tone is an independent choice: Lighter, Normal, or Darker. Normal retains the original neutral values. Success/warning/error meanings and icons stay consistent across every combination.

```html
<html data-app-stylr-theme="dark" data-app-stylr-accent="royal" data-app-stylr-tone="lighter">
```

Use `mint` (Sage), `ember`, `blue` (Slate), `royal`, `amber`, or `monochrome`, with `lighter`, `normal`, or `darker` tones. Set theme, accent, and tone on the same root; repeat all three attributes on independently themed islands. Omitting accent and tone keeps Sage and Normal. Native apps can use `AppStylrTokens.theme(appearance: .dark, accent: .royal, tone: .lighter)` alongside the existing default and accent themes. Display labels come from canonical `accentPresets` and `surfaceTonePresets`; Swift exposes accent labels through `Accents.names`. Apps own any palette switcher and persistence. See [accent palettes and surface tones](../accent-palettes.md).

## Controls and feedback

Import `app-stylr/controls.css` after the tokens and opt in with `data-app-stylr-controls`. The enhanced picker uses matching 12px outer insets and a separate text-to-icon gap. The native fallback retains an arrow allowance. Review legacy select rules that override padding, and exercise keyboard focus, long values, disabled/invalid states, both themes, and phone layouts.

For quieter feedback, use `surface` and `border`, with the semantic color on the icon and text. Existing tinted status-surface tokens remain available. The Reference demonstrates all four quiet states; it does not impose a shared application component library.

## Icons

The recommended base is now a flat charcoal tile with a light product glyph. Keep the identifying symbol and judge it at 16px before scaling up. The example includes a dedicated 16px checkmark; custom products can pass `--source-16` for a compact drawing while larger exports continue to use their master.

```sh
npx app-stylr-icons --source assets/app-icon.svg --source-16 assets/app-icon-16.svg --output public/icons
```

New `icon.background` and `icon.foreground` tokens are exposed in CSS and Swift. The default square fills the 1024px canvas with a 160px radius and transparent corners. The legacy gradient asset and gradient tokens remain available for deliberate compatibility. Icon files do not change with the interface accent. Refresh cached favicon URLs when replacing artwork and check actual browser/installed-app presentation. See [platform icons](../platform-icons.md).

## Reference hosting

The Reference is now an interactive workbench with section navigation, live controls, a token inspector, theme/density/accent/surface-tone controls, and canonical JSON/CSS downloads. Form changes stay in memory; display preferences appear in the URL. No account, upload, telemetry, or browser storage is added.

Use the packaged Reference builder for either a root site or a subpath. Its artifact now includes `workbench.js` and `tokens/` alongside the existing CSS, assets, and manifest. Deploy the whole artifact together. A host pinned to an older package keeps that version until its immutable dependency is updated. See [Reference deployment](../deployment.md).
